sources.name: Open three-sided enclosure
sources.note: The last side is absent. Any proposed closing passage must remain a separate completion hypothesis, rather than becoming observed source evidence.

sources.name: A closed outline with an actual bisector
sources.note: The vertical passage meets the split lower and upper boundary at declared shared sites. The enclosing outline has an interior divider, so its two smaller compartments are the elementary candidates.

sources.name: A closed outline with one inward notch
sources.note: One side turns inward, traverses the inset and returns to the outer level. These are actual connected subchords; the original rectangle is not supplied as an intended face.

sources.name: A closed outline with a sawtooth side
sources.note: Three alternating diagonal excursions occupy one side of a connected enclosure. The repeated reversals may support a local zigzag read without claiming the entire shape is a star.

sources.name: Two closed contours with diagonal sides
sources.note: A three-edge contour and a four-edge contour are spatially separate. Their corners and closures are actual native incidence; no area inventory or polygon name accompanies the public source.

sources.name: A closed contour with distributed outward points
sources.note: The alternating excursions turn around the whole enclosure rather than decorating one roughly straight side. Its native corner sequence can be compared with the sawtooth-side case without an authored star label.
